title: Batcher slot recovery and preemptive drain playbook for continuous batching
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
During a capacity stress window on 2026-02-08 we observed recurring tail-latency spikes and request fairness regressions on the continuous batcher tier that serve multi-tenant hosted workloads. Impact: 10-20% increase in 99th percentile token latency for affected models and observed starvation of low-priority customer routes for ~30 minutes in the most severe cluster.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Emergency throttles applied to burst routing policy to reduce influx to affected hosts.
- Canaryed a reduced batch-window config (from 64ms -> 24ms) which reduced tail spikes but increased overall cost.
- Failed over ~15% of traffic to cold-path replicas with independent batchers.

Root cause hypothesis and evidence:
- Slot allocator lease did not expire reliably under GC/stop-the-world pauses and heavy timer jitter, allowing stale reservations to hold batch slots for >1s.
- The preemption/drain loop assumed monotonic timer progress and lacked a defensive timeout; in the presence of timer drift we saw long-lived slots that blocked batch formation.
- Workload skew amplified fairness issues: priority buckets with high small-request QPS monopolized coalescer windows.
- Logs and flamegraphs point to a small critical path in the slot reclamation goroutine that became CPU-contended under load.

Action items (owner - ETA - status):
1) Implement slot lease with heartbeat and hard-lease expiry at allocator layer - owner: Ethan Zhang - ETA: 2026-02-24 - status: In Development.
2) Add preemptive drain RPC and floor-time on draining loop so a long-running preempt attempt cannot stall formation - owner: Samira Patel - ETA: 2026-02-28 - status: Planned.
3) Instrument per-slot state transitions and add metric suite + alerts for "stale-slot-duration" and "slot-reclamation-rate" - owner: Marco Alvarez (SRE) - ETA: 2026-02-20 - status: In Progress.
4) Create e2e chaos test that simulates timer jitter, GC pauses, and tenant-priority skews; gate on this test in release CI - owner: Jing Wei - ETA: 2026-03-05 - status: Backlog.
5) Rollout plan: canary on 10% of hosts, monitor stale-slot metric and 99th latency for 48h, escalate rollback if either metric regresses >5% from baseline - owner: Ava Martinez - ETA: 2026-03-02 - status: Planned.
6) Short-term config: expose per-tenant max-slot-lease in console and enable default conservative lease for P0/P1 tenants - owner: Product - ETA: 2026-02-22 - status: In Review.
7) Post-release HRT review and cost impact analysis (quantify cost of tighter windows vs latency benefit) - owner: FinOps - ETA: 2026-03-10 - status: Backlog.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Hard-lease expiry vs. keepalive: we chose a hard-lease expiry with optional keepalive because keepalives rely on timers that can also be delayed; hard expiry guarantees forward progress even during pauses.
- Preemptive drain semantics: conservative drains preserve in-flight tokens but may increase latency; we will tune drain window per model class and expose controls to Dedicated customers.
- Cost vs latency: smaller batch windows reduce tail but increase compute; add an Optimize recommendation that suggests quantization/batching mixes per workload to offset this.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests for slot lease paths and simulated timer jumps.
- Integration test harness that replays production request traces with injected timers and GC stalls.
- Canary rollout with metric gates defined in the rollout plan above.

Documentation and runbook:
- Create "batcher-slot-recovery" runbook covering detection, emergency mitigation, and rollback steps. Document will include dashboard queries, Kibana/Logs patterns, and run commands to force lease expiry.

Notes and links:
- Incident dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/continuous-batcher/2026-02-08-incident
- Temporary config change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4219
- Initial investigation notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/2026-02-08+Batcher+Recovery+Investigation

Acceptance criteria for closing ticket:
- Slot lease + preemptive drain merged and deployed to canary and validated against chaos harness.
- Stale-slot-duration alert firing threshold created and shown green for 72h during canary.
- Post-deploy 99th token latency returns to baseline within 5% and fairness regressions resolved in QA trace replay.
